Every query head has its own keys and values. The most to store; each head can retrieve something different.
Two query heads per key/value head: half the cache. Quality usually stays close to multi-head.
All query heads share one: a quarter of the cache, but every head must make do with the same answers —
C · Four maps from two sets of keys
, sequence B: each query head’s attention —
Heads that share keys and values still look at different tokens, because their queries differ. Sharing limits what the heads of a group can retrieve, not what they can ask.
, in every attention of the real model
E · Is writing faster? Measured on this CPU

The cache always halves; the time depends on the hardware. On a GPU, writing waits on reading the cache, so half the cache is close to twice as fast an attention step. On this CPU the step waits on arithmetic instead. PyTorch
path even copies the keys and values first on a CPU, which makes it slower. Sharing without
a copy comes close to plain attention — not below it.
